name: Elkanah
overview: Elkanah was a male member of the tribe of Levi who lived in the villages of the Netophathites. His life and identity are primarily known through his association with this Levitical community, as recorded in 1 Chronicles 9:16. No additional personal notes or attributes are provided beyond these details.
namesAndTitles: The name Elkanah means 'G-d [El] has possessed,' reflecting a theologically rich meaning rooted in the Hebrew language. This proper name is not indicated as being given directly by God but carries significance in expressing divine possession or ownership.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture identifies Elkanah as a descendant of Levi, explicitly linking him to this priestly tribe. He is also inferred to be the son of Asa, establishing a familial lineage within the Levitical context. Beyond these relationships, no further family details are recorded.
scriptureSignificance: Elkanah's significance lies in his role as a Levite residing in the Netophathite villages, which situates him within the priestly heritage central to Israel's worship and covenant identity. His mention in 1 Chronicles 9:16 connects him to the preservation of Levitical genealogies, underscoring the continuity of God's appointed service through the tribe of Levi. While details are scarce, his presence in Scripture affirms the importance of faithful Levitical families in maintaining the spiritual life of Israel.
